plan: My value is $9. I want to avoid overpaying. Since this is round 1 of 1, I need to be conservative. I'll bid slightly above my value, hoping others bid lower. A bid of $9.50 will likely make me exit before higher-value bidders, but still allow me to win if others bid low. I'm aiming to win at a price close to $9.

My value is $9. I want to win only if the price is below $9. Therefore, I want to exit the ascending clock *before* $9. To do this, I need to bid slightly above what I think the other bidders will bid, but still below $9. Given this is the only round, and I have no history, I'll bid conservatively, aiming to win if the others are also conservative. A bid of $5 seems reasonable.

My value is $34. I want to win if the price is below $34 and lose if it's above. To achieve this, I need to bid slightly above what I expect the other bidders to bid, but not so high that I overpay if I win. Since this is the only round, I'll bid conservatively, aiming to win against likely low bids. A bid of $25 seems reasonable.
